Oliver / Ben —

I reviewed the workloads and the spreadsheet. Below is a concise technical comparison and a recommendation matrix so you can weigh procurement speed vs long-term control.

Summary constraints from RegulaHealth: EU residency (Frankfurt), 50–80ms model latency target, sustained 10 QPS with bursts to 60 QPS, separate nightly embedding batch jobs. Strong need for audit logs + HSM/KMS integration.

Option A — Redwood Dedicated (recommended short-term):
- Architecture: Redwood-managed GPU pool in our EU region, tenant isolation at process level, private VPC peering for data egress, control plane hosted by Redwood (we provide SOC2 attestation).
- Node estimate: 3x A100-80GB workers (nvlink enabled) handling steady-state; 1x H100 token-burst worker for peak flattening. Continuous batching + KV prefix cache assumed.
- Latency: median ~30–45ms model-only; 95/99 around 60–110ms depending on request size. Meets your model target.
- Cost: lower TCO initially (reserved commit model). Opex only; no platform license.
- Lead time: 10–21 days for Dedicated provisioning + contract signature.
- Compliance: SOC2 in place (see attachment). We can provide audit log exports to your SIEM via SFTP or streaming.
- Pros: Faster go-to-prod, predictable billing, Redwood manages autoscaling and failures.
- Cons: Control plane resides with Redwood; cannot use customer-managed HSM in initial phase (we can integrate KMS with constraints).

Option B — Private (VPC + on-prem hybrid):
- Architecture: Private control plane (customer-managed credentials), optional on-prem GPU nodes that call local runtime; full VPC isolation.
- Node estimate: 4x A100-80GB equivalent (to allow dedicated scheduling without multi-tenant scheduling optimizations), 1x H100 for burst/quantized inference. Additional node for batch jobs if you run heavy nightly embeddings.
- Latency: model-only median similar when colocated, but depends on your on-prem network and orchestration; introducing customer network increases risk for variance.
- Cost: higher up-front (platform license + provisioning), capital expenditures for on-prem, longer procurement. Lower per-token at scale if fully amortized.
- Lead time: 6–10+ weeks (hardware procurement, firewall rules, KMS/HSM provisioning, audit onboarding).
- Compliance: direct control of keys and logs; preferred for strict audit requirements.
- Pros: Full control, customer-managed HSM, simpler attestation path internally.
- Cons: Longer lead time, greater ops burden, higher initial cost.

Recommendations / Hybrid path:
1) Phase 1 (0–3 months): Start on Redwood Dedicated in EU region with reserved capacity sized as above. This meets timelines and gives you production telemetry. We will enable log-forwarding and set up KMS encryption for data-at-rest.
2) Phase 2 (3–12 months): Run a parallel Private pilot (subset of traffic / nightly batch) and test HSM key exchanges, network rules, and audit export. If pilot metrics (latency variability, ops cost) are acceptable, plan migration cutover.
3) Procurement note: Dedicated contract includes a 6–12 month reserved commit with an option for early termination after pilot iterations. Private requires an enterprise license + deployment package.

Sizing quick numbers (for your 50-token typical reply):
- Dedicated: 3 A100-80GB (workers) + 1 H100 burst (hot) — supports 10 sustained QPS, 60QPS burst with batching; expected token throughput ~250k tokens/minute.
- Private: 4 A100-80GB equiv + 1 H100 — more headroom for isolation and scheduled maintenance windows; add 1 node for batch if jobs run concurrent with peak windows.

Networking & HSM checklist for Private (high risk items):
- Firewall rules allowing our runtime image pulls (if air-gapped, allow image import process).
- HSM/KMS provisioning and key-wrapping workflow; document required APIs and certs.
- Audit log ingestion endpoints and retention SLA.
- Onsite rack power/cooling validation if you host GPUs.

I attached an annotated copy of the spreadsheet with the node math and a quick cost delta (p50). Let us know which path you prefer and we can draft the SOW + procurement timeline.

-Rishi
